text:
## Abstract  
We evaluated whether the GEO Series GSE309890 can be used for a de-novo genome assembly within the BRC Analysis Workflows. Using NCBI’s GEO and SRA programmatic interfaces we confirmed that GSE309890 is an RNA-seq study of *Escherichia coli* K-12 MG1655 comprising six Illumina HiSeq 4000 paired-end runs (SRR36018640–SRR36018645) that together contain 69.1 million read pairs (≈20.7 Gbp).  We next queried the BRC workflow catalogue and found one “Assembly” pipeline, but it is restricted to polishing pre-existing assemblies with long-read data.  No workflow currently accepts short-read RNA-seq data for de-novo genomic assembly, and no transcriptome-assembly pipeline is yet registered.  Therefore, although the raw reads are publicly downloadable and could be processed externally with tools such as SPAdes (genome) or Trinity (transcriptome), they cannot be assembled de-novo inside the BRC workflow system as of this writing.  The data are, however, fully compatible with the BRC “RNA-Seq Analysis: Paired-End Read Processing and Quantification” workflow (`rnaseq-pe-main`) for expression quantification.  These findings inform users that (i) short-read RNA-seq runs are available for local download and custom assembly, and (ii) assembly within BRC will require either long reads or future workflow additions.

## I. Introduction  
Background. GEO Series GSE309890 profiles *E. coli* K-12 MG1655 cultures exposed to the antidepressant sertraline, generating six RNA-seq libraries (paired-end 300 bp).  The requester wishes to “get the raw reads and run an assembly.”  
Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query.  
Knowledge Gap. The availability of raw sequencing data is clear, but it is uncertain whether existing BRC workflows can perform an assembly on Illumina RNA-seq reads.  
Objective & Hypothesis. Objective: determine (i) how to obtain the raw reads underlying GSE309890 and (ii) whether an assembly (genome or transcriptome) can be executed with BRC workflows. Hypothesis: raw reads are accessible via SRA, but current BRC assembly workflows will not support short-read RNA-seq data.

## II. Materials and Methods  
Study Design. We first resolved the GEO Series to its SRA BioProject and enumerated all sequencing runs. We then inspected the BRC workflow catalogue for assembly and transcriptomics pipelines.  
Materials.  
• GEO: queried with `geo_series`.  
• SRA: queried with `ncbi_sra_runs_for_project`.  
• BRC Workflow Registry: queried with `list_workflow_categories` and `get_workflows_in_category`.  
Procedures.  
1. `geo_series(accession="GSE309890", list_files=1)` → confirmed Series metadata and BioProject PRJNA1363958.  
2. `ncbi_sra_runs_for_project(accession="PRJNA1363958", max_results=100)` → retrieved run table for all six SRA runs.  
3. `list_workflow_categories()` → listed top-level workflow areas.  
4. `get_workflows_in_category(category="ASSEMBLY")` and `get_workflows_in_category(category="TRANSCRIPTOMICS")` → identified relevant pipelines.  
Statistical Analysis.  
• Run count = 6 (from SRA run table).  
• Total bases = Σ bases column / n=6 ≈ 20,733,105,300 bp.  
• Mean read length = 300 bp, reported uniformly across runs.  

## III. Results  
### Data Presentation  

Table 1. SRA runs for BioProject PRJNA1363958 (GSE309890)  

| Run accession | Library layout | Read pairs (spots) | Bases | Size (MB) | Download URL (HTTPS mirror) |
|---------------|----------------|--------------------|-------------|-----------|-----------------------------|
| SRR36018640 | Paired | 11,363,329 | 3,408,998,700 | 894 | https://sra-downloadb.be-md.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sos10/sra-pub-zq-1002/SRR036/36018/SRR36018640/SRR36018640.lite.1 |
| SRR36018641 | Paired | 11,997,182 | 3,599,154,600 | 948 | …/SRR36018641.lite.1 |
| SRR36018642 | Paired | 11,992,461 | 3,597,738,300 | 955 | …/SRR36018642.lite.1 |
| SRR36018643 | Paired | 11,720,219 | 3,516,065,700 | 926 | …/SRR36018643.lite.1 |
| SRR36018644 | Paired | 10,415,434 | 3,124,630,200 | 801 | …/SRR36018644.lite.1 |
| SRR36018645 | Paired | 11,621,726 | 3,486,517,800 | 917 | …/SRR36018645.lite.1 |

### Findings  
1. Six paired-end Illumina RNA-seq runs (total 69,110,351 read pairs; ~20.7 Gbp) are available for download via the HTTPS links shown in Table 1.  
2. Workflow inventory shows one Assembly pipeline (`polish-with-long-reads-main`), which requires a pre-existing assembly and long-read data; it does not accept short-read Illumina RNA-seq.  
3. Transcriptomics pipelines (`rnaseq-pe-main`) accept paired-end RNA-seq data and can quantify expression but do not perform de-novo assembly.  

## IV. Discussion  
Interpretation. Raw reads are readily retrievable, satisfying part (i) of the objective. However, current BRC Assembly workflows cannot operate on these data because they expect long reads and an existing assembly.  
Context. GSE309890’s design (RNA-seq on *E. coli* K-12) aligns with the BRC “Transcriptomics” category; the `rnaseq-pe-main` workflow is suitable for read cleaning, alignment to a reference genome, and gene-level quantification.  
Limitations. BRC’s catalogue lacks de-novo assemblers for short-read data and has no dedicated transcriptome-assembly pipelines. Assembly of these RNA-seq reads would require external tools (e.g. Trinity) or future BRC workflow additions.  
Conclusion & Future Directions. Users can:  
a) Download the six SRA runs (Table 1) and perform external de-novo (transcriptome) assembly or genome assembly if complementary DNA-seq exists.  
b) Use BRC’s `rnaseq-pe-main` for expression analysis today.  
c) Monitor BRC workflow updates or request inclusion of short-read assembly or transcriptome-assembly pipelines.

## References  
[1] GEO Series GSE309890 summary. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890  
[2] NCBI SRA run table for PRJNA1363958 (esearch/efetch). https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/efetch.fcgi?rettype=runinfo&retmode=text&retmax=100&WebEnv=MCID_6aac59a655abaee626061d42&query_key=1&retstart=0&db=sra  
[3] BRC workflow catalogue (categories). https://iwc-workflows.github.io/  
[4] Assembly workflow listing (polish-with-long-reads). #workflow/github.com/iwc-workflows/polish-with-long-reads/main/versions/v0.1  
[5] Transcriptomics workflow listing (rnaseq-pe-main). #workflow/github.com/iwc-workflows/rnaseq-pe/main/versions/v1.4  

## Acknowledgments  
We thank NCBI GEO and SRA for primary data access, and the IWC/BRC workflow registry for workflow metadata.
